This project implements a 4-iteration rotation mode CORDIC algorithm that computes the sine and cosine of a 6-bit angle. The angle is loaded via the input pins, and the result is displayed on a 7-segment display, with a DONE flag on the decimal point. It requires a 7-segment display for output and switches or a microcontroller to provide the input angle and start signal. The design is notable for fitting a CORDIC calculator into a single Tiny Tapeout tile.

This project is a trivial first chip that drives three LED segments using three serial flip-flops. It includes a multiplexer selection input and output. Testing is done by probing the LED pins to observe the shifting pattern. No external hardware is required beyond the LEDs. The design is a simple demonstration of sequential logic.

This project is a binary adder that takes input from DIP switches and displays the sum on a 7-segment display. The documentation is placeholder text, so details on the number of bits or exact operation are not provided. It requires a 7-segment display and DIP switches for input. The design is a basic arithmetic demonstration.

This project is a 2-bit full adder with inputs for carry-in, a, and b, and outputs for sum bits and carry-out. The documentation is placeholder text, so testing and usage are not described. It requires input switches and output LEDs to observe the addition results. The design is a fundamental building block for arithmetic circuits.

This design checks if one or more switches are ON on a demo board, displaying the count on a 7-segment display and showing the first letter of the author's name when all are checked. It uses 8 switches as inputs and drives 8 panels of 7-segment displays as outputs. The system includes a reset button to display only the panels whose corresponding switches are ON. It is a simple demonstration of switch monitoring and counting.
